finding: Web Audio processing state and deployment identity are insufficient to prove physical audibility. A direct user gesture may be required before an AudioContext is allowed to transition from suspended to running, and a human observation on the exact physical device remains a separate acceptance layer.

primary_sources.title: Web Audio API 1.1
supports: allowed-to-start may depend on sticky activation
resume remains pending when context is not allowed to start
running state starts rendering but does not prove speaker audibility

primary_sources.title: Auto-Play Policy Changes for macOS
supports: assume audible media requires user gesture
detect denied playback instead of assuming success

artifact.claim_boundary: verified=true confirms only human-observed audibility for the named physical iPhone Safari environment, exact tested commit, and immutable deployment identity. It does not generalize to other devices, routes, volumes, users, or later deployments.

evidence_strength: primary-source-backed contract; deterministic tests authored but not executed in this connector-only run
uncertainty: Current iOS and Safari versions must be recorded at execution time.
AudioContext running state cannot independently establish speaker output.
Human observation is subjective and bounded to one device/output route.
falsification_route: Run the Node tests and retain exact output.
Provide a complete physical-device evidence object with direct gesture, running context, route checks, and human observation.
Demonstrate any accepted object missing a required field or accepting route-active-only evidence; either result falsifies the validator contract.
